results.title: The alpha sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $b$ the *alpha sequence* $U_n=\alpha_b(n)\in\mathbb Z$, $n\in\mathbb N$, is defined by It is integer-valued for every $b$ (its values may be negative when $b\in\{0,1\}$). The matrix drives the recurrence: $M_b\,(U_n,U_{n-1})^{\mathsf T}=(U_{n+1},U_n)^{\mathsf T}$ for $n\ge1$. When an index may be negative, the sequence is extended by $U_{-j}=-U_j$, which is consistent with the recurrence.

results.summary: Let $b>3$ and $a\in\mathbb N$. There is $k>0$ such that $u=\alpha_b(k)$ is odd and $u>2a$; moreover $t=\alpha_b(k+1)$ satisfies $u<t$ and $u^2+t^2=1+but$.

results.title: The alpha formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $X,b,N$, the *alpha formula* $\mathrm{Alpha}(X,b,N)$ is the statement that there are natural numbers $r,s,t,u,v,w,x,y$ satisfying the fifteen conditions (C.2): b>3,\quad u^2+t^2=1+but,\quad s^2+r^2=1+bsr,\quad r2,\quad x^2+y^2=1+wxy,\\ 2X<u,\quad 2X<v,\quad x\equiv X\pmod v,\quad 2N<u,\quad x\equiv N\pmod u . \end{gathered}$$ Here $p\equiv q\pmod M$ means $p\bmod M=q\bmod M$ for natural numbers…

results.title: Soundness of the alpha formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $X,b,N$: if $\mathrm{Alpha}(X,b,N)$ holds then $b>3$ and $X=\alpha_b(N)$.

results.title: Completeness of the alpha formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $b,N$ with $b>3$, the formula $\mathrm{Alpha}(\alpha_b(N),b,N)$ holds; that is, the fifteen conditions have natural witnesses with $X=\alpha_b(N)$. This includes $N=X=0$.
